title: Patch: a background sweep's failing alert says in its issue and email which step stalled and what players notice, and a test finds every alert the server raises
thread:
**Issue #4225 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4225: Patch: a background sweep's failing alert says in its issue and email which step stalled and what players notice, and a test finds every alert the server raises
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The server opens a GitHub issue and emails the owners when one of its background jobs keeps failing. These jobs pair players in the queue, end stalled matches, run the Conquest, co-op, challenge and daily sweeps, and do the hourly clean-ups. For every one of these jobs, the issue and the email explain the alert with one placeholder line saying no description has been written yet. Whoever reads it on a phone has to open the code to learn what broke and how urgent it is. After this change, each alert says which job stalled and what players notice while it does; for the matchmaker, that nobody queued gets a game. A test also fails whenever someone adds a new alert without an explanation.

## Why

- `FailingStreak::new(step)` raises `<step>.failing` with `alert = true` (`crates/server/src/loops.rs:111-146`, #3770). It does so for 15 steps:
  - `matchmaker` (`api/queue.rs:1360`);
  - `matches.reaper`, `seats.reconcile` and `matches.open_reaper` (`api/results.rs:837-840`);
  - the retention loop's seven steps (`api/retention.rs:91-97`);
  - `series.sweeper` (`api/series.rs:690`), `duos.sweeper` (`duos/mod.rs:296`), `challenges.sweeper` (`social/challenges.rs:264`) and `daily.sweeper` (`daily/notify.rs:488`).
- `alerts::meaning` (`crates/server/src/alerts.rs:408-447`) matches whole event names, and none of these 15 is among them. So all 15 get its fallback text, *An alert `alerts::meaning` does not describe yet (crates/server/src/alerts.rs).* That line is the whole explanation in both the public issue (`issue_body`, `alerts.rs:463-477`) and the email (`email_of`, `alerts.rs:485-519`).
- The test meant to prevent this, `every_alert_the_server_raises_says_what_it_means` (`alerts.rs:699-716`), checks a hand-written list of ten names. None of the 15 is on it, so the test passes.
- An alert issue shows only the event name (`loops.rs:112-113`; README, Alerts, `crates/server/README.md:800-815`). So the meaning text is the only explanation the issue carries.
- In the same function, the `loop.crashed` text names six loops (`alerts.rs:411-413`), but `spawn_loops` starts nine (`app.rs:1457-1519`). The challenge, co-op and daily sweepers are missing.

## Proposal

- Add one text per failing step to `alerts::meaning`. Each says:
  - what the step does;
  - what players see while it fails;
  - that it has failed on every pass for at least `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_MS` and `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_PASSES` passes;
  - that the email's `message` field holds the error.
- Like every text there, none names a field of the alert, since the issue is public.
- Add a test that collects every alert name the server's source raises: each `FailingStreak::new` step as `<step>.failing`, each `log_alert` event and each `alert = true` line. It fails on any name whose meaning is the fallback, so the list cannot fall behind the code again. It replaces or extends the hand-written list.
- The `loop.crashed` text names every loop `spawn_loops` starts. Alternatively it names none and points at the email's `loop` field.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/alerts.rs` (`meaning` and its test)
- `crates/server/README.md`, Alerts, wherever it describes these texts
- SPEC §9.5's paragraph on failing sweeps describes operations only and keeps its wording.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each of the 15 steps, the meaning of `<step>.failing` is not the fallback, and it names the step's job. The issue body for `matchmaker.failing` says that queued players are not being paired.
- [ ] The new test reads the alert names from the source. A unit case feeds its checker a made-up step with no text and sees it fail.
- [ ] No text names a profile id, an address, a key or any other field value.
- [ ] The `loop.crashed` text agrees with `spawn_loops`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --lib alerts`, clippy and fmt are green.

## Size and risks

Small: one function's texts and one test, in one or two files. Only the words of alert issues and emails change. There is no behaviour, wire, store or client change, and no ruling. One risk remains: a text can drift from what its step does later on. The test only checks that every alert has a text, not that the text stays accurate.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44842263824)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Every `<step>.failing` alert gets its own `alerts::meaning` text. The 15 steps are `matchmaker`, `matches.reaper`, `seats.reconcile`, `matches.open_reaper`, the retention loop's seven, `series.sweeper`, `duos.sweeper`, `challenges.sweeper` and `daily.sweeper`. Each text names the step's job and what players notice. The `matchmaker.failing` text says queued players are not being paired. Each text says the step has failed on every pass for at least `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_MS` and `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_PASSES` passes, and that the email's `message` field holds the error. None names a field's value.

The `loop.crashed` text names every loop `spawn_loops` starts. A new test reads the alert names out of the server's source and fails on any name that gets the fallback text. A unit case shows the checker failing on a made-up step.

## Files to touch

| Path | Change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/alerts.rs` | change | `meaning` (15 new arms, `loop.crashed` text, fallback const); tests module (replace the hand-written list with the source scan, add unit cases) |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | Alerts section (~line 779 and ~line 812): say each alert's issue and email carry a text, and that a test keeps it so |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `spec/` or any other crate or app. SPEC §9.5/§9 "Failing sweeps" (`spec/09-architecture.md:66`) keeps its wording. No ruling: this is operational, with no behaviour, wire, store or client change.

## Steps

1. **Fallback const.** In `crates/server/src/alerts.rs`, above `meaning`, add `const UNDESCRIBED: &str = "An alert \`alerts::meaning\` does not describe yet (crates/server/src/alerts.rs).";`. Use `_ => UNDESCRIBED` as the last arm. The string stays identical to today's.

2. **Macro for the shared tail.** Above `meaning`, add a `macro_rules! failing_step` that takes `($job:literal, $players:literal)` and expands to a `concat!`. The text is: `$job`, then `" "`, then `$players`, then this fixed tail:
   `" It has failed on every pass for at least \`LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_MS\` and at least \`LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_PASSES\` passes in a row (crates/server/src/config.rs). The email's \`message\` field holds the error."`
   This keeps `meaning` returning `&'static str`. Do not put numbers in the texts, so they cannot drift from the config. Do not put any value from the alert in them.

3. **15 arms.** In `meaning`, before the fallback, add `"<step>.failing" => failing_step!("<job>", "<players>")` for each step below. Refine the wording to read well, but keep the facts, which come from the code:
   - `matchmaker`: "The matchmaker, which pairs queued tickets into matches every few seconds (§9.5), is failing." / "Queued players are not being paired: nobody who queues gets a game." Never write "queued players are not being paired" differently: the test asserts the phrase `not being paired`.
   - `matches.reaper`: "The match reaper, which ends live matches past their ceiling (R79), is failing, or at least one match would not reap." / "Stalled matches are not ended, so their players stay seated and cannot start another game, and rating results wait."
   - `matches.open_reaper`: "The open-room reap (R1450), which deletes rooms nobody joined and starts that never happened, is failing." / "Such rooms keep their room codes and both players, so those players cannot queue or host again."
   - `seats.reconcile`: "The seat reconcile (R1523000), which checks the in-memory seat ledger against the database each reaper tick, is failing." / "A seat left by a game that ended may stay held, so a player is told they are already in a game."
   - `series.sweeper`: "The Conquest series sweeper (R263), which runs the pick clock and starts games a restart left unstarted, is failing." / "Conquest series stall between games: picks never time out and a next game may not start."
   - `duos.sweeper`: "The co-op sweeper, which reaps expired rooms, drops finished actors and folds back live matches with no actor, is failing, or at least one co-op match would not end." / "Co-op rooms and matches may hang instead of ending."
   - `challenges.sweeper`: "The challenge sweeper (B49), which deletes lapsed friend challenges, is failing." / "Lapsed challenges stay listed instead of expiring."
   - `daily.sweeper`: "The daily-games sweeper (§9.13), which expires invites, settles overdue daily games and sends the notices, is failing while the server is awake." / "Overdue daily games are not settled and players are not emailed or pushed about them."
   - `game_records.fold`: "The statistics fold (R1044000), which adds finished game records to the card statistics, is failing." / "Card statistics stop updating, and the purge may hold records it cannot empty."
   - `game_records.refile`: "The record refile (R1596000), which files finished matches whose record never landed, is failing." / "Some finished games may miss the statistics before their log is purged."
   - `retention.purge`: "The retention purge, which deletes old code attempts, match logs, play telemetry and raw game records, is failing." / "Nothing players see yet, but the database keeps growing and old logs stay past their retention."
   - `chat.purge`: "The chat purge (B53), which deletes messages past `CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS`, is failing." / "Old chat messages stay stored past their retention."
   - `duos.logs.purge`: "The co-op log purge, which deletes co-op match logs past `MATCH_ACTION_RETENTION_DAYS`, is failing." / "Old co-op logs and their replays stay past their retention."
   - `idempotency.sweep`: "The idempotency sweep (R2124000), which deletes spend keys past `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_HOURS`, is failing." / "Nothing players see yet: expired keys pile up."
   - `practice.sweep`: "The practice settle sweep (R2422000), which settles practice claims unsettled after `PRACTICE_SETTLE_GRACE_SECONDS`, is failing." / "Practice claims are not paid or refused, so rewards are late."

   `concat!` takes literals only, so write the constant names as plain text. The retention texts ("nothing players see yet") must stay true to what the code does. Re-check each against the doc comment of its function (`reap_stuck_matches` in `api/results.rs`, `seats::try_reconcile`, `duos::sweep`, `daily::notify::sweep`, `fold_pending`, `refile_unfiled`, `purge_expired`, `chat::purge`, `purge_expired_logs`, `sweep_expired`, `sweep_unsettled`, `sweep_series`).

4. **`loop.crashed` text.** `spawn_loops` (`crates/server/src/app.rs:1457-1519`) starts `matchmaker`, `series.sweeper`, `matches.reaper`, `retention.purge`, `challenges.sweeper`, `duos.sweeper`, `daily.sweeper`, `db.heartbeat` (Postgres only) and `bots.pool` (with `LADDER_BOTS`). Rewrite the text to name all nine, in that order, ending "…panicked. The email's `loop` field names it. It restarts by itself, but the panic is a bug." Keep the text free of values. Do not change `loop.returned`.

5. **Checker functions (test module only).** Add these to `mod tests` in `alerts.rs`:
   - `fn alert_names(source: &str) -> Vec<String>`, with no regex (the crate has none), using `str::find`:
     - Each `FailingStreak::new("<lit>")` gives `<lit>.failing`. Find the text `FailingStreak::new("`, read up to the next `"`. `FailingStreak::new(step)` in `loops.rs` has no quote and is skipped.
     - Each `log_alert(` followed by optional whitespace (newlines included) and then `"<lit>"` gives `<lit>`. The `fn log_alert(event: &str…` definition is skipped because its next char is not a quote.
     - For each `alert = true`: take the last `event = ` before it, provided the text between holds no `;`. If that is followed by `"`, the literal is an alert name. `loops.rs:140` (`event = self.failing_event.as_str()`) is skipped.
   - `fn unexplained(names: &[String]) -> Vec<String>` returning every name where `meaning(name) == UNDESCRIBED`.
   - `fn source_alert_names() -> Vec<String>`: walk `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src")` recursively with `std::fs::read_dir` and `read_to_string`, over `.rs` files only. Skip `alerts.rs`, whose own tests raise made-up names. Collect `alert_names` from each, then sort and dedup. A test reading the disk is fine here: `crates/server` is not one of rule 4's pure crates. Check that its `Cargo.toml` and clippy config allow `std::fs` in tests. `src/cli/bot_calibrate.rs` already uses it.

6. **Replace the old test.** Rewrite `every_alert_the_server_raises_says_what_it_means` (`alerts.rs` ~line 699). It keeps its name and loops over the old ten names as before. Add a call to `source_alert_names()`, then:
   - assert it contains all 15 `<step>.failing` names, the 10 old events (the eight literals from `log_alert` calls plus `loop.crashed` and `loop.returned`), so a broken scanner shows up instead of passing an empty list;
   - assert `unexplained(&names)` is empty, with the list in the message.

7. **New unit tests** in the same module:
   - `a_made_up_step_with_no_text_is_found_unexplained`: `unexplained(&alert_names("let mut s = FailingStreak::new(\"made.up\");"))` equals `["made.up.failing"]`. A `log_alert(\n    \"made.up.event\",` source and an `event = \"made.up.crashed\", alert = true` source are found too.
   - `the_scan_skips_what_is_no_literal_alert`: `alert_names` on sources `FailingStreak::new(step)`, `fn log_alert(event: &str, data: Value) {`, `tracing::error!(event = event, alert = true)` and `tracing::warn!(event = "x.y"); foo(alert = true)` returns an empty vec.
   - `every_failing_step_names_its_job_and_what_players_notice`: for the 15 steps, the text contains `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_MS`, `LOOP_FAILING_ALERT_PASSES` and `message`, contains no digit, and is not the fallback. For `matchmaker.failing`, call `issue_body("jackioh.com", Some("abc1234"), &alert("matchmaker.failing", 1_762_776_000_000), 0)` and assert it contains `not being paired` and not the fallback text. The `alert(event, at)` helper already exists in the module.
   - `loop_crashed_names_every_loop_spawn_loops_starts`: read `src/app.rs`, collect each `loops::spawn_supervised("<name>"` literal (the `("name", loops::spawn_supervised("name"` pairs, including those split over lines, e.g. `challenges.sweeper`), and assert `meaning("loop.crashed")` contains each name. This keeps the text honest against `spawn_loops`. Use the same literal-scan style as step 5, and assert at least 9 names were found.

8. **README.** In `crates/server/README.md`, Alerts: in the first paragraph (~line 779), add one sentence that `alerts::meaning` explains each alert in its issue and email, and that `alerts.rs`'s test `every_alert_the_server_raises_says_what_it_means` scans the server's source for each `FailingStreak::new` step, `log_alert` event and `alert = true` line and fails on one with no text. In "A sweep that keeps failing (#3770)", add a sentence that each step's text names its job and what players notice, and that its email's `message` holds the error. Add no ruling and no `spec/pending` file.

## Tests

All are in `crates/server/src/alerts.rs`, `mod tests`:
- `every_alert_the_server_raises_says_what_it_means` (rewritten)
- `a_made_up_step_with_no_text_is_found_unexplained`
- `the_scan_skips_what_is_no_literal_alert`
- `every_failing_step_names_its_job_and_what_players_notice`
- `loop_crashed_names_every_loop_spawn_loops_starts`

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --lib alerts`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Done when

- [ ] All 15 `<step>.failing` texts exist and name the job. The `matchmaker.failing` issue body says queued players are not being paired.
- [ ] The scan test reads names from the source. The made-up-step unit case sees the checker fail.
- [ ] No text holds a value or an id.
- [ ] The `loop.crashed` text names all nine loops of `spawn_loops`.
- [ ] The README is updated.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --lib alerts`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.
- [ ] The harness's `spec check` and `patches check` still pass. If `patches check` or `classify` ask for a fragment, follow the output.

## Risks

- **Scan misses a name.** The scanner is textual. The assertions in step 6 catch an empty or partial scan. A name built at run time (`format!`) would escape it, and today only `loops.rs`'s `<step>.failing` is one, covered by the `FailingStreak::new` literals.
- **Test files in `src` that raise made-up alerts.** Only `alerts.rs` does, and it is skipped. If another file does by then, the scan fails with its name, and the builder must skip or narrow that file rather than give the made-up name a text.
- **`concat!` and backticks.** The text must be string literals only. A `$job` or `$players` argument cannot be a `const`.
- **Drift.** A text can drift from what its step does. The test checks only that a text exists (as the issue notes). The `spawn_loops` check in step 7 does cover the loop list.
- **Public issues.** Do not add a field name beyond `message` and `loop`, nor a value.

## Open questions

None. The decisions already made are: the `loop.crashed` text names every loop (the issue's alternative, naming none, was rejected), and the scan skips `alerts.rs` itself.
```
